name: Snf1/AMPK Energy Sensing Pathway
description: The Snf1 (Sucrose Non-Fermenting 1) kinase in S. cerevisiae is the ortholog of mammalian AMPK and serves as the master energy sensor. Snf1 is activated under glucose limitation by phosphorylation at Thr210 by upstream kinases (Sak1, Elm1, Tos3) and forms a complex with β-subunit Gal83/Sip1/Sip2 and γ-subunit Snf4. Active Snf1 phosphorylates transcription factors (Mig1, Cat8, Sip4) to derepress genes for alternative carbon utilization, gluconeogenesis, and respiratory metabolism. Snf1 is inhibited under high glucose by Reg1-Glc7 phosphatase. The pathway integrates with PKA and TOR to control growth-quiescence transitions based on carbon and energy availability.
scientificAccuracy: Based on extensive research on Snf1/AMPK. All components and mechanisms validated. Highly conserved pathway.
